deliverables.text: A configuration-count table for The Straight Set and The Half-Drop: the total number of distinct, licensable printable configurations available to Thistlebrook from a single engraved cylinder under each scheme, computed by the Fundamental Counting Principle from each scheme's independent choices (licensed colorways, and, for The Half-Drop only, the independent mirror-or-as-drawn state of each alternating column), with the full application of the principle shown for at least one scheme.

A featured-capsule selection table using combinations: for a capsule that recolors a chosen subset of the vine motif's distinct floral elements within one true, fully-repeating tile, compute the number of distinct possible subsets of that size under The Straight Set and under The Half-Drop, with the full binomial-coefficient computation shown for at least one scheme.

A guaranteed-repeat collision analysis: using D1's configuration count as the number of pigeonholes, apply the Pigeonhole Principle to find the minimum number of repeat units Thistlebrook would have to print in a single run before two are guaranteed to show the identical configuration, for each scheme, and compare that threshold to the actual number of repeat units printed in a real production run at Thistlebrook's real fabric width, to state whether a 'no two repeats identical' marketing claim is honest under each scheme.

A setup-dollar synthesis table computing, for The Straight Set and The Half-Drop: (a) total repeat units across Thistlebrook's real printable fabric width multiplied by total repeat units along one engraved cylinder's full rated print run, via the Fundamental Counting Principle (also used as D3's 'actual repeat units printed'), then the cylinder's rated print run converted directly to yards and divided by each scheme's one-time engraving setup cost for the primary metric, and (b) D2's featured-capsule subset count divided by the same setup cost, with the full arithmetic shown for both.

balance.argument_a: Because both schemes share the same engraved-cylinder circumference (set by the motif's 27-inch repeat height, identical for both) and the same sourced screen life (30,000 meters), the two schemes produce identical total printed yardage -- 32,808.4 yards -- from one engraving. The only difference is setup cost: The Straight Set's simpler, uniform-grid engraving costs $650.00 against The Half-Drop's assumed $750.00. On the case's actual primary metric, yards per dollar of setup cost, The Straight Set wins by construction whenever its engraving is cheaper, which it is here: 50.47 yards/$ against 43.74 yards/$.
balance.argument_b: The primary metric measures raw yardage efficiency, not commercial value. The Half-Drop's independent per-column mirror choice makes 8 licensable configurations available from one engraving against The Straight Set's 4 (D1), and its larger true tile supports 66 distinct featured-capsule variants against 15 (D2) -- more than four times the capsule assortment and twice the base configuration count, from a setup that costs only 15% more. If Thistlebrook can sell multiple colorways and capsule variants from the same engraving without re-tooling, The Half-Drop converts a modest cost premium into substantially more monetizable product variety per dollar of setup -- value the primary metric does not capture.
balance.margin_basis: Compare each scheme's primary metric -- total printed yards producible from one engraving (32,808.4 yards, identical for both schemes under the sourced/assumed figures) divided by that scheme's one-time engraving setup cost (Appendix C). Option A: 32,808.4 / $650.00 = 50.47 yards/$. Option B: 32,808.4 / $750.00 = 43.74 yards/$. Option A wins by 13.3%.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Which end of the sourced 30,000-50,000 meter screen-life range (S3) to use for both schemes
modeling_assumptions.basis: S3 states a range, not a single figure, and does not break the range out by pattern type (straight vs. offset). No source ties a specific figure within the range to either scheme specifically. The low end is used so the primary metric is not inflated by an optimistic assumption.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Scales both schemes' total yardage -- and therefore both schemes' yards-per-dollar figure -- by the same proportion. Because both schemes share the same rated print run in this model, this choice does not change which scheme wins the primary metric or the size of the margin between them; it only changes both absolute figures together.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: One-time engraving/setup cost, in USD, for each scheme
modeling_assumptions.value_used: The Straight Set: $650.00. The Half-Drop: $750.00 (a $100 premium).
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public, dated 2026 price list for rotary-screen engraving could be located. S2 is a real, named engraving vendor's own price list, but it is dated 2011 and does not break pricing out by straight-grid vs. offset/half-drop repeat -- only by repeat size and color count. The $650/$750 figures are stated scenario values informed by S2's real (if dated) per-screen range, with a modest premium assumed for The Half-Drop on the stated basis that its offset lattice requires tighter cross-column registration during engraving than a uniform grid.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The case's answer is sensitive to this value -- a Hero who argues the registration premium is unrealistically large or small has found the case's real fault line.
